source_documents.title: Tetracoordinate-Boron-Rigidified Heterohelicenes with Fragment-Precise Short-Range Charge Transfer for Narrow Near-Infrared Emission

reference_evidence_units.quote: According to this law, a contraction in the optical energy gap (ΔEopt) triggers an exponential acceleration in the nonradiative decay rate (knr) (eq 1).
reference_evidence_units.subject: design
reference_evidence_units.statement: Energy-gap law framing of the NIR problem.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Coupled with the rigidified skeleton, the alternating donor−acceptor arrangement enables fragment-precise short-range charge transfer with drastically suppressed nonradiative decay.
reference_evidence_units.subject: B2N5, B4N10, B6N15
reference_evidence_units.statement: Rigidity plus short-range CT suppress knr.

reference_evidence_units.quote: spatial demand synergizes perfectly with the alternating D−A imposed LR-CT constraint, drastically rigidifying the molecular skeleton to suppress nonradiative decay. Consequently, B2N5 delivers an exceptional 100% PLQY featuring thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) at 561 nm.
reference_evidence_units.subject: B2N5

reference_evidence_units.quote: Notably, the delayed-fluorescence component decreases as the temperature is raised from 150 to 298 K, a hallmark of TADF behavior (Figure S5b).
reference_evidence_units.subject: B2N5
reference_evidence_units.statement: Delayed component (2.1 us) with temperature dependence; RISC 1.67e7 s-1.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Consequently, its PLQY plummets to 3% in air due to severe oxygen quenching of the triplet states.
reference_evidence_units.subject: B2N5
reference_evidence_units.statement: Triplets are on the emission pathway.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In contrast, B4N10 and B6N15 display monoexponential, nanosecond-scale lifetimes (9.0 and 9.4 ns, respectively), with negligible temperature dependence (Figures 3d, S5d and S5f), which is unambiguously characteristic of prompt fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.subject: B4N10, B6N15
reference_evidence_units.statement: No TADF in the NIR members.

reference_evidence_units.quote: It also severely restricted the excited-state vibrational modes and the corresponding Huang−Rhys factors, thereby narrowing the emission to a fwhm of 0.09 eV.
reference_evidence_units.subject: B4N10
reference_evidence_units.statement: Extension suppresses the vibronic coupling that drives knr and broadening (PLQY 34% at 724 nm).

reference_evidence_units.quote: From B2N5 to B4N10, the number of low-frequency vibrational modes with HRFs > 0.5 decreases from five
reference_evidence_units.subject: B2N5 vs B4N10
reference_evidence_units.statement: Fewer strongly coupled modes in B4N10.

reference_evidence_units.quote: suggesting that multiple-helicene extension effectively suppresses aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ).
reference_evidence_units.subject: B4N10, B6N15
reference_evidence_units.statement: PLQY of B4N10 barely changes with doping; B2N5 drops.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Prompt NIR emission (724 nm, PLQY 34%) explained against the energy-gap law by suppressed vibronic coupling (fewer large Huang-Rhys modes).

environment_context: doping concentration in PMMA: PLQY nearly unchanged from 1% to 20% (ACQ suppressed) (E09)

contrast_group.varied_factor: helicene extension (two vs four tetracoordinate borons)
contrast_group.paper_difference: B2N5 is a visible TADF emitter (100% PLQY under N2, 3% in air); B4N10 emits prompt NIR fluorescence at 724 nm with 34% PLQY, explained by suppressed vibronic coupling against the energy-gap law.
